chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who visits the House before shaving, he said: It is not befitting unless he is forgetful. } }, {

Then he said: Indeed, people came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) on the day of sacrifice, and some of them said: O Messenger of Allah, I shaved before I slaughtered; and some said: I shaved before I threw (the pebbles). So they did not leave anything that it was befitting for them to delay except that they brought it forward, so he said: There is no harm.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim shaves his head before throwing the pebbles during Hajj?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between 'not befitting' (la yanbaghi) and 'sinful' (haram) regarding the sequence of Hajj rituals, establishing that minor deviations do not invalidate the pilgrimage. It links the Imami ruling directly to the Prophetic precedent, where the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his progeny) declared 'no harm' (la haraj) upon companions who had prematurely shaved or thrown pebbles, emphasizing ease in religious practice. This supports the Shia juristic principle that the prescribed order is recommended but not strictly obligatory for validity.
